newsitem.title: UK: Port state controls agreed for Mediterranean.
newsitem.headline: Port state controls agreed for Mediterranean.

text.p: Eight Mediterranean countries have agreed to introduce port state controls, the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) said.
A memorandum of understanding has been signed by the maritime authorities of Malta, Cyprus, Turkey, Algeria, Egypt, Israel, Morocco and Tunisia, it said.
Port state controls require countries' maritime authorities to inspect at least 15 percent of ships entering their ports in any year.
Poorly maintained vessels are detained for repairs.
The IMO said it welcomed the move as a further step towards ensuring implementation of international shipping conventions and treaties.

The Mediterranean agreement will allow for an interim period of two years before full implementation, it added. That would allow time for the IMO and the European Commission to train surveyors and inspectors in the signatory countries.

Representatives from India and Nigeria attended the Valetta meeting at which the Mediterranean agreement was signed. They are interested in developing similar agreements in the Indian Ocean and in West and Central Africa, the IMO said.
Port state control agreements have already been set up in Europe, Latin America, Asia and the Pacific and in the Caribbean.

IMO secretary general William O'Neil said, "Port state control adds to the efforts of flag states to improve maritime safety and to prevent maritime pollution. That is why IMO is fully involved in these efforts and is extending experience globally so that substandard operators will have fewer places in which to hide."
